Your task is summarize the modifications made in the patch.
Your summary should consist of two parts, modifications in each file and their relationships.

From 2d19c3fd80178160dd505ccd7fed1643831227a5 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Robert Hancock <robert.hancock@calian.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Jan 2022 15:41:32 -0600
Subject: [PATCH] net: axienet: increase default TX ring size to 128

With previous changes to make the driver handle the TX ring size more
correctly, the default TX ring size of 64 appears to significantly
bottleneck TX performance to around 600 Mbps on a 1 Gbps link on ZynqMP.
Increasing this to 128 seems to bring performance up to near line rate and
shouldn't cause excess bufferbloat (this driver doesn't yet support modern
byte-based queue management).

Fixes: 8a3b7a252dca9 ("drivers/net/ethernet/xilinx: added Xilinx AXI Ethernet driver")
Signed-off-by: Robert Hancock <robert.hancock@calian.com>
Signed-off-by: David S. Miller <davem@davemloft.net>

diff --git a/drivers/net/ethernet/xilinx/xilinx_axienet_main.c b/drivers/net/ethernet/xilinx/xilinx_axienet_main.c
index b4f42ee9b75d..377c94ec2486 100644
--- a/drivers/net/ethernet/xilinx/xilinx_axienet_main.c
+++ b/drivers/net/ethernet/xilinx/xilinx_axienet_main.c
@@ -41,7 +41,7 @@
 #include "xilinx_axienet.h"
 
 /* Descriptors defines for Tx and Rx DMA */
-#define TX_BD_NUM_DEFAULT		64
+#define TX_BD_NUM_DEFAULT		128
 #define RX_BD_NUM_DEFAULT		1024
 #define TX_BD_NUM_MIN			(MAX_SKB_FRAGS + 1)
 #define TX_BD_NUM_MAX			4096
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/net/ethernet/xilinx/xilinx_axienet_main.c`**
   - The default transmission (TX) ring size was changed from `64` to `128`. This modification is made in the definition of `TX_BD_NUM_DEFAULT`.

### Relationships

- The change in the TX ring size is aimed at improving the transmission performance of the AXI Ethernet driver on ZynqMP platforms. The previous default size of `64` was identified as a bottleneck, limiting performance to around 600 Mbps on a 1 Gbps link. By increasing the size to `128`, the performance is expected to approach line rate, addressing the performance issue without introducing excessive bufferbloat. This patch is a follow-up to a previous commit (identified by the fix tag) that added the Xilinx AXI Ethernet driver, indicating that the modifications are part of ongoing improvements to the driver’s performance.
